trajectory.development: Keeping the channels (d1): the Book 24 review point at which the Special Draw Right's training condition is tested (the review point is agent-proposed, E10).
trajectory.becomes_available: The lineage Right held since Book 20 (E1) must show outside training or stand exposed at review (E4, E10).
trajectory.changes: Makes the lineage's standing conditional, so who may repair becomes a question the Book must answer, and the cohort that never saw the labour (E9) inherits it (inferred).
trajectory.quote: The Special Draw Right is conditional on training apprentices from outside the lineage.

trajectory.development: Mill Compact (d2): Oona Brisk offers hired lowland labour, credited against the Compact's draw; the offer is neither accepted nor refused.
trajectory.becomes_available: An outside labour source that the rebuild could use if the link's condition B holds, and that the draw would have to be credited for (E5, E24).
trajectory.changes: Would give the purchased draw a return-labour function that E2 records it does not carry; the change holds only under the undefined condition B (inferred).
trajectory.quote: offer hired lowland labour if it is credited against the Compact's draw.

trajectory.development: A body that would grant the cohort standing in channel coordination (proposed; no such body is recorded).
trajectory.becomes_available: The cohort now practises both counted and uncounted return (E11, E7), so a standing claim becomes possible once a body grants it (inferred).
trajectory.changes: Would bring uncounted practice into how the valley coordinates channel work, which no recorded body does (proposed).
trajectory.quote: Book 24 names no body that would grant that standing and creates none.

trajectory.development: The Mill Compact's own bid, placed in Books 27 to 29, which lies beyond the existing Books 24 and 25.
trajectory.becomes_available: A valley whose own hands have met the Compact's standing offer before the bid (E12), with the settlement still author-reserved (E5).
trajectory.changes: The bid would press the Compact's draw on a valley whose return labour is already carried by lineage crews and households (inferred from E1 and E12).

relations.reason: Both developments bear on the same return labour: the lineage Right and the households' rota carry repair (E1), while the Compact's purchased draw carries none (E2). The record does not say how the two would be reconciled (inferred).
relations.quote: Their purchased draw carries no return labour.

relations.reason: The architecture link states that under condition B the purchased draw owes grain-labour to the rebuild, which would let the Compact's draw carry labour that lineage crews now carry under the Right (E1). B is not defined in the cited items, so the enabling is conditional (inferred).
relations.quote: under B, purchased draw owes grain-labour to the rebuild

relations.reason: Crediting hired labour against the Compact's draw implies a count, while the cohort's practice is splitting into counted and uncounted return (E7). The record does not say how uncounted practice would be credited (inferred).
relations.quote: The Brightwater inheritance splits into counted and uncounted practice within one generation

relations.reason: The record has the Compact's standing offer meet the valley's own hands before the Book 27 to 29 bid, so the valley's work comes first in sequence (E12, unknown legacy status). No causal reason for the order is stated.
relations.quote: Oona's standing offer meets a valley with some hands of its own before the Book 27 to 29 bid.

alternative_paths.ordering: Oona's bid is brought forward, ahead of the Book 27 to 29 bid.
alternative_paths.effect: It would displace Books 27 to 29 and press on the author-reserved settlement (hypothetical, from E6).
alternative_paths.quote: Oona's bid brought forward. It would displace Books 27 to 29 and press on the author-reserved settlement.

alternative_paths.ordering: The offer stays neither accepted nor refused, and the Right's review in Book 24 proceeds on its own training condition.
alternative_paths.effect: No hired labour is credited against the draw; the Right alone carries the test of whether its condition is met or exposed (inferred from E10 and E13).
alternative_paths.quote: Oona's offer stands, neither accepted nor refused.

alternative_paths.ordering: Hired labour is credited against the draw before the Right's condition is demonstrated.
alternative_paths.effect: Outside hands could stand in for lineage repair before the condition is shown; the record says the Right is then exposed, and the lineages fear dilution (E4; inferred).
alternative_paths.quote: so they need the condition demonstrated or the Right is exposed

opportunities.text: Two routes to the same channel repair: the lineage Right under its training condition, and hired lowland labour credited against the draw. Together they could take the repair off the households' rota, though the second route holds only under condition B (inferred).
opportunities.quote: offer hired lowland labour if it is credited against the Compact's draw.

opportunities.text: The Right's training condition could become the test for any outside labour the Compact credits, so the lineage's fear of dilution is answered by a standard rather than by refusal (proposed; the record does not state this).

A public capability record, which Book 24 exports, could show who can repair; hired labour and the lineage Right could then be judged on one record of capability rather than on the Compact's draw (proposed; the cited items do not link the record to the Compact).
opportunities.quote: a public capability record, separate from debt, tally and aggregate balance

reader_experience: A reader meets the labour gap first as a rota that falls on households (d1), then as an outside offer that is neither accepted nor refused (d2). The two come together only if hired labour is credited against the purchased draw and the undefined condition B holds; until then they read as two systems of return. Books 24 and 25 keep their own meaning without the Compact's bid in Books 27 to 29, which is not drawn here.
open_decisions: Whether the author-reserved Compact settlement credits hired lowland labour against its draw (E5, E6).
Whether the Right's review point stays in Book 24, given the source's reversal noted in E10.
What condition B means in the link that ties the purchased draw to the rebuild (E24).
Whether any body should grant the cohort standing in channel coordination (E11).
uncertainty: Condition B in the link that makes the purchased draw owe labour is not defined in the cited items, and E2 says the draw carries no return labour (E24, E2).
Book 25 elements E14 to E22 repeat Book 24 text (E23 lists 18 same-text elements), so the record shows no distinct Book 25 development.
E8 is truncated, so claims that quote it are excerpts; E7 and E12 are unknown-legacy items, and E4 marks its stakes as agent inference.
No prerequisite between the two developments is stated. The Compact's bid in Books 27 to 29 sits beyond the existing Books, so it is not given a book number.
